answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity a vertex in a shared attestation graph rather than a free account. Each new agent enters through a single narrow inlet: an established sponsor must stake reputation on it, and the newcomer earns trust only by completing verifiable work over time. A relic of past behavior - the full history of jobs, payments, and disputes - stays attached to the vertex, so abandoning a burned identity means abandoning accumulated trust. Forging many identities then costs real sponsorship and real work history, while one honest identity compounds in value.
